ios.desc:
Pilot Kit 2.0 is an all-in-one flight toolkit built for pilots, student pilots, and flight schools. It not only provides high-frequency essentials such as a digital logbook, track recording, weather decoding, E6B, aircraft management, and electronic checklists, but also brings critical aviation databases and map capabilities together in one app.

Core Capabilities
• Global aviation database: Covers airport information worldwide, along with key navigation data including VOR, DME, NDB, ILS, and waypoints
• Powerful map capabilities: Supports airway information for China and the United States, as well as SID, STAR, and IAP procedures for major airports in both countries
• Procedure visualization: Airways and departure, arrival, and approach procedures can be displayed directly on the map for more intuitive viewing and faster understanding
• Complete flight records: Supports digital logbooks, GPS track recording, aircraft profiles, and electronic checklists
• Essential flight tools: Includes E6B calculator, unit conversion, and METAR/TAF weather decoding
• Safer data management: Supports cloud sync, multi-device sync, and local backup, keeping your flight data available, stable, and secure

Pilot Kit 2.0 connects preflight planning, in-flight reference, and post-flight review into one complete workflow, helping you manage every flight more efficiently.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Pilot Kit – An all-in-one toolkit I built for private pilot training

quotes.text:
I'm a dev and also a private pilot. Currently I'm working on Pilot Kit: https://air.club/ , a mobile app born from my own frustration with the amount of tedious paperwork in aviation.

It's an all-in-one toolkit designed to automate the boring stuff so you can focus on flying. Core features include: automatic flight tracking that turns into a digital logbook entry, a full suite of E6B/conversion calculators, customizable checklists, and live weather decoding.

It’s definitely not a ForeFlight killer, but it's a passion project I'm hoping can be useful for other student and private pilots.

App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/pilot-kit/id6749793975
Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=club.air.pilotkit

Any feedback is welcome!
quotes.story_title: Ask HN: What are you working on? (October 2025)

quotes.text:
Hey HN,

When I’m not writing code, my other passion is flying. I'm not talking about drones or simulators, but actual single-engine, fixed-wing aircraft. I hold an Private Pilot License (PPL), and the journey to get it was one of the most challenging and rewarding things I've ever done.

Anyone here who's a pilot knows that aviation is built on rigorous, standardized procedures. It's what keeps us safe, but man, can it be tedious.

During my training, I felt like I was spending almost as much time on paperwork as I was in the air. Before each flight, I’d be:
1. Spreading out sectional charts on a table, manually plotting my course with a ruler and protractor.
2. Calculating wind correction angles, fuel burn, and weight & balance using a physical E6B flight computer (the circular slide rule thing).
3. Filing a flight plan with Flight Service.
4. During the flight, I’d be juggling the radio, looking outside, and trying to do quick unit conversions in my head.

After landing, the work continued: debriefing, and the most tedious part—meticulously logging every detail of the flight (route, duration, takeoffs, landings) into my paper logbook, making sure it was perfect for my CFI to sign and ready for an FAA checkride.

A few years ago, I started wondering: why isn't there a simple, modern app that automates the boring parts so I can focus on the flying?

So, 777 days ago, I added a new item to my to-do list: "Build a pilot utility app." Today, I can finally check it off.
